2: General term in the expansion of \(\left(y^{1/5} + x^{1/10}\right)^{55}\) is given by \(T_{r+1} = {}^{55}c_{n}\left((x)^{1/10}\right)^{r}\left(y^{1/5}\right)^{55-r}\), i.e. \(T_{r+1} = {}^{55}c_{r}\,x^{10}\cdot y^{11-r/5}\). Clearly \(T_{r+1}\) will be free from radical signs if \(r/5\) and \(r/10\) are integers for \(0 \leq r \leq 55\). Therefore \(x = 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50\), which is 6 terms.

5: When 7 is at the 10000th place, there are 9 choices for each of the remaining places, so the total possible ways is \(9^{4}\). When 7 is not at the 10000th place, then there are four possibilities for the digit 7; the 10000th place can be filled in 8 ways and the remaining in 9 ways, so the total possibility \(= 4 \times 8 \times 9^{3}\). Hence the total number of ways is \(9^{4} + \left(4 \times 8 \times 9^{3}\right) = 41 \times 9^{3}\).
